Android from the foundation · Puzzle 7 of 15

Letters between apps

Apps can't reach into each other, but they can ask the town hall to deliver a request. The town hall checks whether the app is allowed first.

The problem

In puzzle 6, the sandbox kept every app inside its walls. But a chat app still opens the camera, and a link in a message opens the browser. If apps can't reach each other, how do they work together?

See it

Save this diagram as a GIF

The building block

An app sends an Intent: a message to system_server asking it to open a screen, in another app or in your own. It travels by Binder, like every message to the town hall.

Some actions need a permission: a right the app has to be granted, like using the camera. Some are granted at install, others the user grants while the app runs. system_server checks them before it acts. It knows which app sent the Intent from the app's UID, which Binder tells it (puzzle 13 shows how).

The analogy

You can't walk into the neighbour's house, but you can send the town hall a letter: "please open the photo room for me". The town hall checks its list of who's allowed what, then passes it on, or sends it back.

Check yourself

A game sends an Intent asking to open the camera, but the user never granted it the camera permission. What happens?

Right. system_server checks the sender's permissions before acting.

Not quite. The kernel guards files and memory. Permissions for actions are checked by system_server.

Not quite. Delivery isn't automatic: the town hall checks permissions first.

Why does an Intent go to system_server instead of straight to the other app?

Not quite. Size has nothing to do with it: the sandbox means only the town hall can deliver.

Right. Only the town hall can deliver between sandboxes, and it checks the sender on the way.

What's the difference between the sandbox and a permission?

Not quite. The sandbox is walls the kernel enforces for every app; permissions are rights system_server grants per action.

Right. Walls by the kernel; rights by the town hall.

What you now know

An Intent is a letter to the town hall: "open this screen". system_server checks the sender's permissions, then delivers it, or doesn't.
